findings.reason: the wrappers carry real fixture defaults (bound 0.25 T, per-pair scale and tolerance, the static column map) and the plan's §2 done-when is interface parity in the solver, which a fixture-side builder satisfies; the honest remedy is a code simplification, not a design change.
findings.text: fixture_constraint_pairs wraps centroid_constraint_pair (:63) and level_constraint_pair (:141), each of which is a thin constructor of a ConstraintPair over an already-existing functional plus an already-existing unknown; the three levels add surface over the two-element tuple it returns and no stated reason is given why the generic assembly (constraint.py `constraint_response_matrix` :731 / reduced_newton.py `derive_reduced_constraint_pairs` :2569) cannot be extended instead

findings.reason: the two builders differ in both scope and unknown (response-derived CircuitCurrentUnknown on a machine vs a bounded static exterior field on a coil-less fixture), so the fork is by design; and the column convention is consumed once by the fixture driver, which the plan does not extend — a single-source-of-truth repair worth landing, but not a change to what the plan builds.
findings.text: `_centroid_pair` already builds a ConstraintPair over CurrentCentroidConstraint for centroid conditioning, and the plan adds a second centroid-pair constructor at scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/centroid_row.py:63 rather than extending a shared constructor in the owner module nova/equilibrium/constraint.py:934; additionally `_field_direction` (centroid_row.py:41) re-encodes the column ordering declared at scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py:69 as literal tuples, so a change of convention in the one declared source would silently mis-map the driver's columns

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the compensating family is one protocol (CompensatingUnknown) and one functional protocol (ConstraintFunctional) hiding the bound, damped-step, refusal and dual-flux-image behaviour behind interfaces smaller than what they carry; the solver sees a tuple of ConstraintPair, and the one substantive new module is the owner (constraint.py), not a spread of parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — a second centroid-pair constructor is added as fixture-side glue beside the existing one; the direction convention it encodes is also declared in a second file.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan's §1 cites and §2 extends the existing constraint machinery in nova/equilibrium/constraint.py (CurrentCentroidConstraint :934, ConstraintPair/ConstraintBinding, CompensatingUnknown Protocol :159) and nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py (derived constraints), adding only the two new implementations BoundedExteriorFieldUnknown and FluxLevelConstraint rather than a parallel subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the fixture adds three concentric builders over the same ConstraintPair construction and a static direction map, without stating why the existing pair-assembly path cannot carry it.
